bacterial_spot.cause_of_disease: This disease comes from tiny germs (bacteria) that get into the leaves through small cuts or natural openings. You can see small dark wet-looking spots with yellow rings around them. The germs spread through dirty seeds, splashing water, old plant waste, and tools that were not cleaned.
bacterial_spot.recommendation: Pull off and throw away the spotted leaves. Try not to splash water on the leaves when you water the plants. Always use clean seeds and wipe your tools between plants. If needed, a copper spray can help — just follow what the label says.

early_blight.cause_of_disease: This disease is caused by a fungus that lives in old plant waste left on the ground. It usually shows up first on the older leaves near the bottom as brown round spots that look like a target. The spots grow bigger over time and the leaves start turning yellow.
early_blight.recommendation: Pick off the sick lower leaves and try to keep the leaves dry. Give the plants more space so air can move around them. Put mulch on the ground to stop dirt from splashing up. If it keeps spreading, use a fungicide as the label tells you.

late_blight.cause_of_disease: This is a very serious disease caused by a fast-moving mold. It makes big brown wet-looking patches that can spread very quickly. The tiny spores fly with the wind and can move from plant to plant in just a few days.
late_blight.recommendation: Act fast by pulling out badly sick leaves or whole plants. Do not put them in your compost pile. Keep leaves dry and move sick plants away from healthy ones. Talk to a local farming expert about what spray to use to save the rest of your crop.

septoria_leaf_spot.cause_of_disease: This disease is caused by a fungus that mainly goes after the leaves. It starts near the bottom of the plant as many tiny round grey-brown spots with dark edges. It spreads when rain or watering splashes the fungus from old plant waste onto the leaves.
septoria_leaf_spot.recommendation: Take off the spotted lower leaves and try not to get water on the leaves when you water. Let more air flow around the plants and clean up old plant scraps from the ground. If the spots keep showing up, use a fungicide spray and follow the directions on the bottle.
